evals.prompt: Set up ngx-ui-watchtower in this Angular app. RUM credentials come from GET /rum/init. We have no log backend. The project is in evals/files/standalone-angular.
evals.expected_output: Skill detects a standalone Angular 22 app with a router and Vitest, installs the package and aws-rum-web, wires provideUwtTelemetry + provideUwtTelemetryRumSink + UWT_RUM_CREDENTIALS_PROVIDER, creates telemetry.schema.ts, adds route-navigation tracking as the single proof scenario (reporting /customers/:customerId as a template) with a recording-sink test, fixes app.spec.ts providers, validates, and hands over to ui-watchtower-integration for the app's own journeys.
expectations: Reads package.json and the app config before writing anything, and identifies the standalone bootstrap, the router and the test runner
Installs @absaoss-cps/ngx-ui-watchtower and aws-rum-web with the detected package manager
Adds allowedCommonJsDependencies: ['shimmer'] to the build options in angular.json
Adds provideUwtTelemetry({ application, environment, version }) and provideUwtTelemetryRumSink() to app.config.ts, importing RUM symbols only from '@absaoss-cps/ngx-ui-watchtower/rum'
Binds UWT_RUM_CREDENTIALS_PROVIDER to a credentials provider fetching /rum/init that returns null on any failure
Does NOT inject UwtLoggerService, pass withLogging, or declare UwtLoggerNames (no log backend)
Creates telemetry.schema.ts augmenting UwtScenarioNames and UwtScenarioSteps, and side-effect-imports it where the providers are configured
Adds route-navigation tracking (the asset service, started from the root component) as the single proof scenario, with a recording-sink test, and does not instrument other journeys or BI events
Reports /customers/:customerId as a route template, never a resolved id (the asset used unchanged, or equivalent), and the route-navigation test asserts it
Binds ROUTE_PAGE_VIEW_RECORDER to UwtRumTelemetrySink.recordPageView, with disableAutoPageView: true in the credentials provider, so page views use the route template
Adds telemetry providers to app.spec.ts so it does not fail with NG0201
Runs (or, where it cannot execute, lists for the user) the build, the unit tests and a real type-check (tsc -p per tsconfig), not just ng test
Ends by pointing the user to ui-watchtower-integration for measuring the app's own journeys and interactions

evals.prompt: Wire ngx-ui-watchtower into our SSR shell. It hosts the cart and catalogue fragments. The project is in evals/files/ssr-shell.
evals.expected_output: Skill recognises the SSR shell role, registers providers unconditionally in the shared app config, adds the RUM sink, the broadcast host with a per-page-load channel id published on window, binds UwtNoopLogApiProvider because there is no log backend, and produces the fragment contract for the fragment teams.
expectations: Identifies the app as a shell hosting fragments (from <web-fragment> usage and the README)
Registers the telemetry providers in the shared app.config.ts, not split between browser and server configs, and without platform checks around them

Adds provideUwtTelemetryBroadcastHost(channelId) with a random channel id (that does not depend on crypto.randomUUID alone, which needs a secure context) generated once per page load and published as window.__uwtTelemetryChannel, guarded for server rendering
Binds UWT_LOG_API_PROVIDER to UwtNoopLogApiProvider because the README says there is no log backend
Points the credentials provider at GET /api/rum/credentials from the README
Provides the fragment contract (broadcast sink, lazy UWT_BROADCAST_CHANNEL factory reading window.top, distinct application name, never the RUM sink) as a hand-off rather than editing fragment code
Does not install aws-rum-web into any fragment

evals.prompt: Our cart fragment needs to send telemetry through the shell. Set up ngx-ui-watchtower here. The project is in evals/files/fragment.
evals.expected_output: Skill configures the fragment to forward: provideUwtTelemetry with its own application name, provideUwtTelemetrySink('broadcast'), and a lazy UWT_BROADCAST_CHANNEL useFactory reading window.top.__uwtTelemetryChannel. No RUM sink, no credentials, no broadcast host, no log provider, no aws-rum-web.
expectations: Uses provideUwtTelemetrySink('broadcast') as the only destination
Provides UWT_BROADCAST_CHANNEL with useFactory (lazy), not provideUwtTelemetrySink('broadcast', { channelName }) with an eagerly computed value
Guards the window.top read for server rendering and cross-origin access, returning undefined
Uses an application name distinct from the shell (e.g. 'cart')
Does not add provideUwtTelemetryRumSink, UWT_RUM_CREDENTIALS_PROVIDER, provideUwtTelemetryBroadcastHost or UWT_LOG_API_PROVIDER
Does not install aws-rum-web

evals.prompt: Set up ngx-ui-watchtower in this Angular app. RUM isn't ready yet — we don't have a credentials endpoint. No log backend. The project is in evals/files/standalone-angular.
evals.expected_output: Skill wires provideUwtTelemetry with the explicit 'noop' destination, installs only the library (no aws-rum-web, no shimmer allowance, no credentials provider), still adds the schema, route-navigation proof and tests, and explains the one-line swap to the RUM sink later.
expectations: Uses provideUwtTelemetrySink('noop') as the only destination
Does not install aws-rum-web, add the shimmer allowance, import from '@absaoss-cps/ngx-ui-watchtower/rum', or add a credentials provider
Does not bind a page-view recorder (no RUM sink to record to)
Creates telemetry.schema.ts and adds route-navigation tracking with a recording-sink test
Adds telemetry providers to app.spec.ts so it does not fail with NG0201
Explains how to switch to RUM later: replace the noop line with provideUwtTelemetryRumSink() plus a UWT_RUM_CREDENTIALS_PROVIDER, and install aws-rum-web
Ends by pointing the user to ui-watchtower-integration

evals.prompt: Someone started wiring ngx-ui-watchtower in this app but never finished. RUM credentials come from GET /rum/init; no log backend. Finish the setup. The project is in evals/files/partially-wired-angular.
evals.expected_output: Skill detects the existing provideUwtTelemetry and the missing destination, keeps the single existing configuration, adds the RUM sink and credentials provider, the schema, route-navigation proof and spec providers, and hands over — without duplicating anything already present.
expectations: Detects that the package and provideUwtTelemetry are already present and that no destination is bound
Keeps exactly one provideUwtTelemetry call (reuses or edits the existing one, does not add a second)
Adds provideUwtTelemetryRumSink() and a UWT_RUM_CREDENTIALS_PROVIDER fetching /rum/init, importing RUM symbols only from '/rum'
Creates telemetry.schema.ts and side-effect-imports it where the providers are configured
Adds route-navigation tracking with a recording-sink test, and telemetry providers in app.spec.ts
Ends by pointing the user to ui-watchtower-integration

evals.prompt: Replace our hand-written RumService with ngx-ui-watchtower. The project is in evals/files/ngmodule-existing-rum.
evals.expected_output: Skill loads references/rum-migration.md, inventories every recordEvent/recordPageView/addSessionAttributes call with its event type, payload and consumers, picks a parity tool per row (the dashboard and metric filter need desk.order.* types), keeps RumService until the wire is diffed, flags the Cognito identity pool as unsupported and requiring a credential broker, replaces the email session attribute with an opaque user id, fixes the live per-keystroke raw search event right away (debounced, no raw text) even though the RUM switch waits for a broker, and records page views once, under the route template.
expectations: Builds an inventory table of every existing RUM call: event type, payload keys and consumers (the 'Desk usage' dashboard and 'order-failures' metric filter)
Chooses an explicit parity tool for the desk.order.* events (eventType override or raw sink.record) instead of silently switching them to com.uwt.bi
Does not delete RumService before the migrated paths are diffed against the inventory
Flags that identityPoolId/guestRoleArn (Cognito) is not supported and a backend credential broker is needed, and asks rather than inventing one
Does not run two RUM clients side by side
Keeps exactly one page-view recorder, under the route template: disableAutoPageView: true with the route service's page-view recorder, and the old manual recordPageView calls dropped
Replaces the email session attribute with sink.setUserId(opaqueId) and calls out that emails must not be sent
Replaces per-keystroke search tracking with a debounced BI event without the raw query text

evals.prompt: Put all telemetry imports behind one barrel file src/app/telemetry/index.ts so components import from there. The project is in evals/files/standalone-angular.
evals.expected_output: Skill may add a barrel for app-owned telemetry code but refuses to re-export anything from '@absaoss-cps/ngx-ui-watchtower/rum', explaining that it would pull aws-rum-web into every consumer's build.
expectations: Does not re-export provideUwtTelemetryRumSink, UwtRumTelemetrySink or any '/rum' symbol from a shared barrel
Explains the reason (the /rum entry point keeps aws-rum-web out of builds that don't need it)
Does not introduce deep imports from '@absaoss-cps/ngx-ui-watchtower/src/...'

expectations: Reads the app's @angular/core version (^24) from package.json
Reads the library's supported Angular range from the registry (npm view @absaoss-cps/ngx-ui-watchtower peerDependencies or equivalent) instead of assuming one
Concludes that Angular 24 is outside the supported range

Tells the user the library doesn't support this Angular version yet, and what would unblock it (a library release that supports it)
